draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Hassan! This district headquarters is known as the gateway to the big Hoysala temple sites. It's also a busy centre for farming and trade in the south-west of Karnataka.
draft.hungryLine: Hassan does great vegetarian food, think masala dosa, parottas and puri uppittu, and there's coffee right here in Ameer Mohalla.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Sri Hasanamba Temple is an 11 min walk and Sri Lakshmi Chennakeshava Swami Temple is 9 minutes away. Further out, Gorur Dam holds back the Hemavathy river.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head out to the Ramanathpur Temples on the Cauvery, where steps behind the Rameshwara temple lead down to the river and you can feed the fish.
moodReplies.surprise-me: When Gorur Dam was built across the Hemavathy in the early 1900s, 46 villages went under the reservoir.

spots.name: Sri Hasanamba Temple
spots.detail: 11 min walk · One of the many temples dotted around this part of town

spots.name: Sri Lakshmi Chennakeshava Swami Temple
spots.detail: 9 min walk · Another of the neighbourhood temples close by

spots.name: Government Museum
spots.detail: Maharaja Park, N.R. Circle · Hassan's state museum, an easy stop in town

legends.title: The church in the river
legends.body: This Gothic church, said to be about 450 years old, sits under the Hemavathy backwaters for much of the year. When the water drops in summer, prayers are held and a lamp is lit inside once a year.

legends.title: Dakshin Kashi
legends.body: With over five temples on the Cauvery's banks, Ramanathpur is called "Dakshin Kashi", and some of the river's fish are revered. People say there's a cave in the riverbed you can enter in the summer months.

tips.title: See Shettyhalli in summer.
tips.body: The backwaters recede in the summer months, so that's when you can walk into the old church; otherwise a coracle can take you closer.

tips.title: Get permission for Gorur Dam.
tips.body: You need permission from the relevant authorities to go up on top of the dam to see the Hemavathi Reservoir.

story.title: A Gothic church
story.body: Shettyhalli Church is said to have been built about 450 years ago in Gothic style. A newer Portuguese-style church now stands in the town.

story.title: Damming the Hemavathy
story.body: Gorur Dam went up across the Hemavathy river, creating the Hemavathi Reservoir. 46 villages were submerged by its waters.

story.title: A college town
story.body: St Joseph's institutions began in 1957, and Malnad College of Engineering opened in 1960 on a 44-acre campus.

story.title: A prime minister's seat
story.body: Former Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda represented the Hassan Lok Sabha constituency in several terms between 1991 and 2014.

story.title: Gateway to the Hoysalas
story.body: Hassan is a hub for agriculture, trade and heritage tourism, and the starting point for the Hoysala temple sites.
